title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GUS'S BIG TOAST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gus, a roofer from Worcester, Massachusetts.
Gus is not afraid of heights. Forty feet up on an icy roof? No problem.
But one phone call scared him half to death.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PHONE CALL
segments.quote: Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear, not absence of fear.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: His little brother Nicky was getting married, and wanted Gus as best man. With a speech.
Gus said, let me think. Then he hid in his truck for an hour.
In his glove box sat an overdue library book by Mark Twain. It said:
Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear, not absence of fear.
So brave people get scared too? Gus called Nicky back. Yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ELEVEN PAGES
segments.quote: I have made this letter longer than usual, only because I have not had the time to make it shorter.
segments.author: Blaise Pascal
lines: That night he wrote every story since nineteen seventy-nine.
Eleven pages. His wife Linda said, Gus, it's a wedding, not a miniseries.
She showed him a line from Blaise Pascal, a French thinker:
I have made this letter longer than usual, only because I have not had the time to make it shorter.
So Gus took the time. Eleven pages became one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE ROOF CREW
segments.quote: Practice is the best of all instructors.
segments.author: Publilius Syrus
lines: He practiced out loud. In the shower. To the dog. The dog left the room.
His foreman, Big Lou, had a line from the Roman writer Publilius Syrus taped in his hard hat:
Practice is the best of all instructors.
So every lunch break, Gus gave the speech to five roofers. By Friday, they were clapping.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE REHEARSAL
segments.quote: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: At the family dinner, Gus read the speech off his phone.
Flat as a line at the DMV. Aunt Gloria nodded off in the mashed potatoes.
The bride, Dana, whispered a line from Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
Gus put the phone away and told it like he meant it. Aunt Gloria woke up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE MICROPHONE
segments.quote: Silence at the proper season is wisdom, and better than any speech.
segments.author: Plutarch
lines: Wedding night. Two hundred faces. Gus took the mic, and his mind went blank.
Then he remembered his mom's favorite line, from the Greek writer Plutarch:
Silence at the proper season is wisdom, and better than any speech.
So he didn't rush. He took a breath and looked at his little brother. The room got quiet, and warm.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TOAST
segments.quote: Keep your eyes wide open before marriage, half shut afterwards.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: Then the words came back: the kid brother who followed him everywhere, and found his own way.
He raised his glass with advice from Benjamin Franklin:
Keep your eyes wide open before marriage, half shut afterwards.
Everybody laughed. Dana laughed hardest. Nicky cried. And Gus sat down a hero.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be brave. Keep it short. Practice. Mean it. Breathe. Love.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be scared and do it anyway. Keep it short. Practice out loud. Mean it. Breathe. And keep your eyes half shut.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And if you need a best man, I bring my own bow tie.
